summary: Alfred Horsford Bingley worked in the fields of Indology and history/archaeology. He was educated at Kensington School and studied at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst around 1884–1885.
Alfred Körte studied at the University of Bonn (~1886–1890) and worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held posts at Bonn, Greifswald, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig (~1917–1934).

Indologist Alfred Louis Noël de Sadous studied under Eugène Burnouf (~1840–1847) and earned his dr.-ès-lettres at the University of Paris (~1845–1847). He served as a teacher (troisième) at Lycée Hoche.

Alfred Ludwig was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Weber, Boeckh, and Haupt, completing his Habilitation at the University of Vienna (1858). He was subsequently a professor of classical philology and comparative linguistics at Charles University (1860–1901).

Alfred Master, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford. He held lecturing and governing posts at SOAS (1937–1960) and served as Assistant Keeper at the India Office Records (1951–1957).

Philosopher Alfred North Whitehead studied at the University of Cambridge and Trinity College. He held academic posts at Cambridge (1884–1910), Imperial College London (1914–1924), and Harvard University (1924–1937).

Alfred Nottrott, who worked in linguistics and Indology, studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1860) and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Leipzig (~1885–1887). In 1867, he served as a missionary with the Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church.

Alfred Radcliffe-Brown studied at the University of Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers. He held posts at the University of Sydney (~1925–1931), University of Chicago (~1931–1937), University of Oxford (~1937–1946), and Fundação Escola de Sociologia e Política de São Paulo.

Alfred Roussel, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied under Abel Bergaigne and Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Fribourg from 1903 to 1920.

Linguist Alfred Schmitt completed his Ph.D. at the University of Rostock under Gustav Herbig and Hermann Güntert. He held posts at Rostock (1928–1935), the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1935–1941), and as ordinary professor at the University of Münster (1941–1956).

Alfred Shenington Geden, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies and Indology, earned degrees from Oxford and Aberdeen. He served as Principal of Royapettah College (1886–1889) and held professorships at Richmond College (~1891–1922) and Wesleyan College (1891–1915).

Indologist and linguist Alfred William Stratton studied under Maurice Bloomfield at Johns Hopkins (Ph.D. 1895). He taught at the University of Chicago (1895–1899) before serving as Principal of Oriental College and holding a post at the University of the Punjab.

Alfred von Gutschmid studied at Leipzig (Ph.D. 1854) and Bonn under Christian Lassen, working in history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held professorships at Kiel (1863–1873), Königsberg (1873), Jena (1876), and Tübingen (1877).

Linguist Alfredo Trombetti graduated from the University of Bologna (~1887–1891). He spent his academic career there, becoming ordinary Professor of Semitic Philology in 1904 and Professor of Glottology in 1912.
Ali Beth was an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Utrecht University (~1937–1943) under the supervision of Jan Gonda. He later taught J. A. B. van Buitenen.

Indology and religious studies scholar Ali S. Asani completed his education at Harvard College and Harvard University. Beginning around 1983, he became a professor at Harvard University, holding named chairs in Middle Eastern and Indo-Muslim and Islamic studies.

Linguist Alice Harris completed her studies at Harvard University and the University of Massachusetts Amherst. She held academic positions at Vanderbilt University (~1979–2002) and at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~2009).

Alice Margaret Stevenson was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell at Somerville College. She earned degrees from Trinity College Dublin (M.A., Sc.D.) and the University of Oxford (M.A.).
Alice Y. Tseng, who works in Japanology, history, and archaeology, was a graduate student under Eugene Y. Wang. She was attested as a professor at Boston University in 2013.

Alicia Turner works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago (2000–2009) under Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, and became an Associate Professor at York University in 2009.
